Haven & Stone.

Sanctuaries carved from silence.

A private-acquisition real estate site for ultra-exclusive geological residences — monolithic, moody, and built to read as an invitation to a private collection rather than a listing.

Full Website Design
Concept & Intent

The thinking
behind the brand.

I wanted to move away from the warmth of Altitudes and design something colder and more architectural — a site for residences framed as rare objects, where restraint, dark materiality, and negative space do the persuading instead of lifestyle photography.

This project was an opportunity to design for exclusivity rather than access: a permanent collection of two residences, a materials study, a "Reserved for the Few" privacy section, and an acquisition-request form in place of a standard contact form — every choice built to feel selective rather than welcoming.

How this differs from Altitudes — same luxury-residence brief, deliberately different execution: Altitudes is warm timber and daylight, built for alpine chalets people actually live in, while Haven & Stone is colder and more geological — architecture staged as a private acquisition rather than a home, with the site built around an inquiry-only request form instead of an open booking flow.
